Lessons.Title: Use Multiples to Find Equivalent Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 original Grade4 Unit2 Lesson10: use multiples of numerators and denominators to explain equivalent fractions numerically, bridging earlier unit-fraction bars and number lines. Retain learning goal and existing examples when correct.
Warm-up Notice and Wonder, 10 minutes: 1/3=2/6, 2/3=4/6, 3/3=6/6, 4/3=8/6; each numerator and denominator doubled, original fraction value unchanged. Partner explains the pattern.

Activity1 Elena's Way, 20 minutes: 1/5→2/10,3/15,4/20,5/25,10/50 using common multipliers2,3,4,5,10; relate to Andre's subdivided number lines. Generate FIVE distinct equivalent fractions to1/8 with any positive whole-number multipliers greater than1, e.g.2/16,3/24,4/32,5/40,7/56. Teacher checks generated equations and peer language.

Activity2 Equivalence Hunting, 15 minutes: test the exact original pairs 5/2 versus10/8 (NO, different values) and2/6 versus4/12 (YES, both1/3). Then inspect all12 original candidate fractions for equivalence to3/4; exactly7 are equal: 6/8,30/40,12/16,15/20,24/32,75/100,60/80. Other5 are non-equivalent. Source novel denominators9,16,32,40,80 support generalization but are not treated as stand-alone high-stakes facts.

Lesson synthesis10 minutes: (a×n)/(b×n)=a/b for nonzero positive multiplier n. Clarify that the two numbers change while the fraction's quantity does not. Teacher prompts students to explain, not merely select an answer.

First-party Edulytics independent formative five-minute Cool-down (not source protected publisher prompt): find two distinct equivalents of1/8; explain both why5/2 and10/8 are not equivalent and why2/6 and4/12 are. Teacher marks open explanation, exact numeric Practice is supplementary.

KeyConcepts.Title: Common multiplier
KeyConcepts.Definition: The same positive whole-number factor applied to numerator and denominator.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent share
KeyConcepts.Definition: Fractions that describe identical position/value despite different numerals.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Both parts must be scaled equally.

KeyConcepts.Title: Not equivalent
KeyConcepts.Definition: Fractions generated by unequal scaling or otherwise differing value.

WorkedExamples.Title: Elena's1/5
WorkedExamples.Question: Find two different equivalents of1/5.
WorkedExamples.Method: Multiply both numerator and denominator by same factor.

WorkedExamples.Title: Hunting for3/4
WorkedExamples.Question: Which original candidate fraction6/8 or12/15 equals3/4?
Steps: 6/8=3/4 because both numerator and denominator divide2.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Multiply numerator and denominator by different numbers.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Different scaling changes the rational value.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assume an unfamiliar denominator implies equivalence.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Several distractors in the source list are NOT equivalent to3/4.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Check exact products for each candidate.

SummaryPoints: All original four warm-up equations and five Elena equivalent forms are represented.
Exactly five new equivalent fractions for1/8 are student-generated.
Original Equivalence Hunting two pairs and complete 12-candidate list, with exactly seven equal to3/4.
Existing exact numeric Practice checks equivalence; student diagrams and full written explanations are teacher-reviewed.
First-party five-minute formative is separate from source-protected publisher Cool-down.
